# CLI reference

Version 1.13 · 2026-11-20

Every `kongtrol` command, in the same groups and order as `kongtrol --help`. Every command has its own help with examples: `kongtrol <command> --help`. Español: [CLI.md](CLI.md). First time: [SETUP.md](SETUP.md).

## Connection

### `kongtrol up`

Connects the given profiles and opens the live view; the VPNs stay connected when you close it. Next: kongtrol status.

```text
kongtrol up [profile...] [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--alert-bell` | ring bell on critical alerts |
| `--all` | connect all configured profiles |
| `--dry-run` | simulate connection flow and checks without changing system state |
| `--fav` | connect saved favorite profiles |
| `--group group` | connect all profiles in the group |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol up office
kongtrol up --group work
kongtrol up office --dry-run
```

### `kongtrol down`

Disconnects the given profiles and restores your DNS when the last tunnel drops. Next: kongtrol status to confirm.

```text
kongtrol down [profile...] [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--all` | disconnect all active tunnels |
| `--group group` | disconnect all profiles in the group |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol down office
kongtrol down --group work
kongtrol down --all
```

### `kongtrol status`

Shows each tunnel with its state, IP and traffic. If one fails: kongtrol doctor.

```text
kongtrol status [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--alert-bell` | ring bell on critical alerts |
| `-w, --watch` | auto-refresh every 2 seconds |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol status
kongtrol status --watch
kongtrol status --json
```

### `kongtrol routes`

Shows which destinations go through each tunnel, or through one if you name the profile. With --system: the system routes Kongtrol added.

```text
kongtrol routes [profile] [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--system` | show the system routes Kongtrol added (if one is missing: kongtrol reload) |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol routes
kongtrol routes office
kongtrol routes --system
```

### `kongtrol dashboard`

Opens the dashboard to set up and connect your VPNs from the browser; starts Kongtrol in the background if needed. If it doesn't open, copy the address shown.

```text
kongtrol dashboard [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol dashboard
```

## Setup

### `kongtrol init`

Guides you step by step to add your VPNs, policies and security to kongtrol.yaml. At the end it checks the helper (offers to install it) and asks whether to connect now.

```text
kongtrol init [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `-y, --yes` | at the end, install the helper and connect without asking |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol init
kongtrol init --yes
KONGTROL_LANG=es kongtrol init
```

### `kongtrol config`

Groups the commands to validate kongtrol.yaml, turn protection on or off (kill switch, DNS guard, public IP lookup) and set language, favorites, default group and dashboard on this computer. Start with: kongtrol config validate.

```text
kongtrol config [command]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config validate
kongtrol config killswitch on
kongtrol config lang en
```

### `kongtrol config validate`

Checks kongtrol.yaml and explains each error with how to fix it, without connecting anything. If it passes: kongtrol up.

```text
kongtrol config validate [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config validate
kongtrol config validate --json
```

### `kongtrol config favorites`

Saves the profiles you use most on this computer so you can connect them together. Next: kongtrol up --fav.

```text
kongtrol config favorites [command]
```

Aliases: `fav`

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config favorites add office
kongtrol config fav list
```

### `kongtrol config favorites list`

Shows the favorite profiles saved on this computer. To connect them: kongtrol up --fav.

```text
kongtrol config favorites list [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config favorites list
```

### `kongtrol config favorites add`

Marks the profile as a favorite on this computer. Next: kongtrol up --fav.

```text
kongtrol config favorites add <profile> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config favorites add office
```

### `kongtrol config favorites remove`

Removes the profile from your favorites; the profile stays configured. To check: kongtrol config favorites list.

```text
kongtrol config favorites remove <profile> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config favorites remove office
```

### `kongtrol config default-group`

With no argument it shows the group kongtrol up connects on this computer when you name no profiles; with a group, it saves it. Next: kongtrol up.

```text
kongtrol config default-group [group] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config default-group
kongtrol config default-group work
```

### `kongtrol config lang`

Saves the message language on this computer; KONGTROL_LANG takes priority. To try it: kongtrol --help.

```text
kongtrol config lang <es|en> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config lang en
kongtrol config lang es
```

### `kongtrol config dashboard`

Changes where the dashboard listens on this computer only, without touching kongtrol.yaml. To see it: kongtrol config dashboard show.

```text
kongtrol config dashboard [command]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config dashboard show
kongtrol config dashboard set-port 9090
```

### `kongtrol config dashboard show`

Shows the dashboard address and port on this computer and where they come from. To change them: kongtrol config dashboard set-port.

```text
kongtrol config dashboard show [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config dashboard show
```

### `kongtrol config dashboard set-port`

Saves the dashboard port on this computer; it applies the next time Kongtrol starts. Next: kongtrol down --all and kongtrol up.

```text
kongtrol config dashboard set-port <port> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config dashboard set-port 9090
```

### `kongtrol config dashboard set-bind`

Saves the address the dashboard listens on; 127.0.0.1 lets only this computer see it. It applies when Kongtrol starts again.

```text
kongtrol config dashboard set-bind <address> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config dashboard set-bind 127.0.0.1
```

### `kongtrol config dashboard reset`

Clears the address and port saved on this computer and goes back to kongtrol.yaml. It applies when Kongtrol starts again.

```text
kongtrol config dashboard reset [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config dashboard reset
```

### `kongtrol config audit-log`

With no options it shows where the log is, how many days are kept, the size of each file, the total space and how much it uses now. Older days are deleted on their own at start, when a file fills up and every midnight; past the total space the oldest go first. With Kongtrol open the change applies at once; otherwise it is saved in kongtrol.yaml.

```text
kongtrol config audit-log [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--days int` | days kept, today included (1 to 365; 0 = 30) |
| `--max-size-mb int` | largest size of one file in MB (1 to 1024; 0 = 100) |
| `--max-total-mb int` | largest space of all files together in MB (1 to 10240; 0 = 500) |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config audit-log
kongtrol config audit-log --days 30
kongtrol config audit-log --max-total-mb 500 --max-size-mb 100
```

### `kongtrol config public-ip`

Off by default. When on, Kongtrol asks an external service (api.ipify.org by default) for your public IP, and that service sees it; only when a tunnel connects or disconnects and when you ask (kongtrol ip). The kill switch and DNS guard do not need it.

```text
kongtrol config public-ip <on|off> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config public-ip on
kongtrol config public-ip off
```

### `kongtrol config killswitch`

The kill switch prevents leaks: if a protected VPN drops without you disconnecting it, Kongtrol blocks what went through it until it is back. With Kongtrol running it applies at once; otherwise it is saved in kongtrol.yaml.

```text
kongtrol config killswitch <on|off|status> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config killswitch on
kongtrol config killswitch status
```

### `kongtrol config dns-guard`

The DNS guard keeps your DNS lookups from leaking outside the VPN: while VPNs are connected, Kongtrol uses only their DNS. With Kongtrol running it applies at once; otherwise it is saved in kongtrol.yaml.

```text
kongtrol config dns-guard <on|off|status> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config dns-guard on
kongtrol config dns-guard status
```

### `kongtrol config update-check`

Off by default. When on, Kongtrol asks api.github.com at most once a day for the latest published version; GitHub sees your IP and "kongtrol/<version>", nothing else. If there is a newer one it tells you (tray, dashboard, kongtrol version and status). It never downloads or installs: you update with your installer or package manager.

```text
kongtrol config update-check <on|off|status> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config update-check on
kongtrol config update-check off
kongtrol config update-check status
```

### `kongtrol config recent-connections`

On by default. Kongtrol notes which addresses this computer connected to in the last hour, which VPN each one went through and which program opened it. The list lives only in Kongtrol's memory: it is never saved to disk or logs, never leaves this computer, and is erased when you turn it off or close Kongtrol.

```text
kongtrol config recent-connections <on|off|status> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol config recent-connections status
kongtrol config recent-connections off
kongtrol config recent-connections on
```

### `kongtrol profile`

Creates VPN profiles without questions (for scripts), imports WireGuard or OpenVPN files and finds the VPN apps on this computer. Step by step with questions: kongtrol init or the dashboard (kongtrol dashboard).

```text
kongtrol profile [command]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol profile detect
kongtrol profile add nordvpn --name home --country Spain
kongtrol profile import office.conf --create
```

### `kongtrol profile import`

Checks the file with the same rules as the dashboard (no scripts or commands; an .ovpn with its certificates inside) and saves it in ~/.kongtrol/configs/ for your user only. It does not replace a file with the same name unless you pass --overwrite. With --create it also creates the profile that uses it (name: the file's, or --name). Next: kongtrol up <name>.

```text
kongtrol profile import <file.conf|file.ovpn> [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--create` | also create the VPN profile that uses the file |
| `--name string` | name of the saved file, without extension (default: the file's own) |
| `--overwrite` | replace a file imported earlier with the same name |
| `-y, --yes` | with --create, restart Kongtrol without asking to use the new profile |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol profile import ~/Downloads/office.conf --create
kongtrol profile import provider.ovpn --name home
kongtrol profile import office.conf --overwrite
```

### `kongtrol profile add`

Creates a profile like "＋ Add" in the dashboard, with the same rules. <type>: forticlient, openvpn, protonvpn, nordvpn, surfshark, ciscoanyconnect, wireguard, globalprotect, tailscale or cloudflarewarp. The password never goes on the command line: if the type uses one, it is asked without showing it in a terminal; otherwise add it in the dashboard. If Kongtrol is running, it offers to restart it to use the profile. Next: kongtrol up <name>.

```text
kongtrol profile add <type> [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--app-path string` | path of the official app, if it is not in its usual place |
| `--auth-method string` | certificate, credentials or certificate+credentials (default: the usual one for the type) |
| `--cert string` | client certificate file |
| `--city string` | server city (NordVPN, Proton VPN) |
| `--config-file string` | the profile's WireGuard .conf, or OpenVPN .ovpn / .conf file |
| `--country string` | server country (NordVPN, Proton VPN) |
| `--group string` | NordVPN server group |
| `--host string` | VPN server address (FortiClient, Cisco, GlobalProtect) or exit node (Tailscale) |
| `--interface string` | the VPN's network interface name, if Kongtrol does not recognize it on its own |
| `--key string` | the certificate's private key file |
| `--name string` | profile name (required), for example office |
| `--no-auto-connect` | do not connect the app automatically: Kongtrol opens it and waits for you to connect |
| `--port int` | VPN server port |
| `--protocol string` | protocol (Proton VPN) |
| `--server string` | exact server (NordVPN, Proton VPN) |
| `--username string` | VPN username (the password is asked separately, never here) |
| `--wait-timeout string` | how long to wait for you to connect in the app (for example 5m) |
| `-y, --yes` | restart Kongtrol without asking to use the new profile |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol profile add nordvpn --name home --country Spain
kongtrol profile add forticlient --name work --host vpn.mycompany.com --username ana
kongtrol profile add wireguard --name office --config-file ~/.kongtrol/configs/office.conf
```

### `kongtrol profile detect`

Lists the VPN apps it finds (the same as the dashboard and kongtrol init) and the profile type for each. It only looks for files: it opens no app and connects to nothing. Next: kongtrol profile add <type> --name <name>.

```text
kongtrol profile detect [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol profile detect
kongtrol profile detect --json
```

### `kongtrol policy`

Adds or removes policies (which sites, IPs or apps go through which VPN), shows which VPN each destination uses and why, and tests lists of destinations. Start with: kongtrol policy list.

```text
kongtrol policy [command]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol policy add github.com --via office
kongtrol policy show github.com
kongtrol policy test targets.txt
```

### `kongtrol policy add`

Creates a policy like "＋ Add" in the dashboard: a site or link (and its subdomains), an IP or a range (10.0.0.0/8) or an app (app:chrome.exe) go through the --via VPN. The name is generated (for example "github.com via office") unless you pass --name. With --block-when-down that traffic does not leave through the normal internet while the VPN is off. Next: kongtrol policy show <site>.

```text
kongtrol policy add <site|ip|range|app:<exe>>... [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--block-when-down` | if that VPN is off, block the traffic instead of using the normal internet |
| `--name string` | policy name (default: "<first target> via <vpn>") |
| `--no-subdomains` | only the exact site, without its subdomains (*.site) |
| `--via string` | VPN profile the traffic goes through (required) |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol policy add github.com --via office
kongtrol policy add https://intranet.mycompany.com 10.20.0.0/16 --via work --block-when-down
kongtrol policy add app:teams.exe --via work --name teams
```

### `kongtrol policy remove`

Removes the policy with that name (kongtrol policy list shows them). It asks first; for scripts: --yes. That traffic goes back to the normal internet.

```text
kongtrol policy remove <name> [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `-y, --yes` | remove without asking (for scripts) |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol policy remove "github.com via office"
kongtrol policy remove teams --yes
```

### `kongtrol policy list`

Shows your policies with their VPN and resolved IPs. For one destination: kongtrol policy show <target>.

```text
kongtrol policy list [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol policy list
kongtrol policy list --json
```

### `kongtrol policy show`

Shows which policy and which VPN a destination (domain or IP) or an app uses, and why. To see them all: kongtrol policy list.

```text
kongtrol policy show <target|app:<exe>> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol policy show github.com
kongtrol policy show 10.20.30.40
kongtrol policy show app:chrome.exe
```

### `kongtrol policy test`

Reads a file with one destination (IP or domain) per line and shows which VPN each would use. If something looks wrong: kongtrol policy show <target>.

```text
kongtrol policy test <file> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol policy test targets.txt
kongtrol policy test targets.txt --json
```

### `kongtrol reload`

Loads kongtrol.yaml into the running Kongtrol: policies and connected tunnels, or only one profile or group. If you added profiles, it offers to restart Kongtrol. Next: kongtrol status.

```text
kongtrol reload [profile] [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--group group` | reload only the active tunnels of this group |
| `--policy` | reload only the policy engine (skip groups) |
| `-y, --yes` | if Kongtrol needs a restart, restart without asking |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol reload
kongtrol reload office
kongtrol reload --yes
```

### `kongtrol restart`

Stops Kongtrol and starts it again with kongtrol.yaml re-read; reconnects the VPNs that were connected. Same as the dashboard's Restart button. Next: kongtrol status.

```text
kongtrol restart [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol restart
```

### `kongtrol export`

Prints a kongtrol.yaml template without passwords in the terminal, to use on another computer or hand to your colleagues. Kongtrol sends it nowhere: you decide where to keep it. To save it to a file: kongtrol export > template.yaml.

```text
kongtrol export [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol export
kongtrol export > template.yaml
```

## Diagnostics

### `kongtrol doctor`

Checks everything Kongtrol needs without connecting any VPN and says how to fix each problem. To apply safe fixes and install the helper if missing: kongtrol doctor --fix.

```text
kongtrol doctor [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--fix` | apply safe fixes and install or update the helper if needed |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol doctor
kongtrol doctor --fix
kongtrol doctor --json
```

### `kongtrol ip`

Looks up your public IP once with an external service (api.ipify.org by default) and compares it with the expected IPs. Works only if you turned it on: kongtrol config public-ip on. If it finds a leak: kongtrol doctor.

```text
kongtrol ip [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol ip
kongtrol ip --json
```

### `kongtrol traffic`

Commands to see where your traffic goes.

```text
kongtrol traffic [command]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol traffic recent
```

### `kongtrol traffic recent`

Lists the destinations of the last hour: name (when a policy resolved it) or IP, port, program, which VPN it went through (or direct) and how many connections there were. Needs Kongtrol open. The data lives only in memory and never leaves this computer. Turn it off with: kongtrol config recent-connections off

```text
kongtrol traffic recent [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--limit int` | How many destinations to show (0 = all) |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol traffic recent
kongtrol traffic recent --limit 20
kongtrol traffic recent --json
```

### `kongtrol logs`

Shows the latest events from the audit log, or from the background process with --daemon. To follow them live: kongtrol logs -f.

```text
kongtrol logs [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--daemon` | show the background daemon's log (daemon.log) instead of the audit log |
| `-f, --follow` | follow events live |
| `--level level` | filter by level (INFO\|WARN\|ERROR\|SECURITY) |
| `--profile profiles` | filter by profiles (several: repeat the flag or separate them with commas) |
| `--since day` | from this day (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--tail N` | show the last N events (default `100`) |
| `--until day` | up to this day, included (YYYY-MM-DD) |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol logs
kongtrol logs -f --profile office
kongtrol logs --daemon
```

## System

### `kongtrol service`

The helper makes the network changes that need admin rights, so you never open an admin terminal. Install it once: kongtrol service install.

```text
kongtrol service [command]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol service install
kongtrol service status
kongtrol service uninstall
```

### `kongtrol service install`

Installs the helper as a system service; it asks for admin permission once. Next: kongtrol service status.

```text
kongtrol service install [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol service install
```

### `kongtrol service uninstall`

Removes the helper; without it Kongtrol can't change routes or DNS. To install it again: kongtrol service install.

```text
kongtrol service uninstall [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol service uninstall
```

### `kongtrol service status`

Shows whether the helper is installed, responding and on this version. If it's missing or outdated: kongtrol service install.

```text
kongtrol service status [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol service status
```

### `kongtrol uninstall`

Disconnects your VPNs, closes Kongtrol, removes the network helper, the autostart entry and the PATH entry its installer added. It deletes the app only when install.sh or install.ps1 installed it; if it came from a package manager (Homebrew, npm…) or the Windows installer, it tells you how to finish. Your data is only on this computer: Kongtrol keeps nothing online or anywhere else. With no options it stays here, so everything comes back if you reinstall: the ~/.kongtrol folder (VPNs, settings, imported files, logs) and your passwords in this computer's system keychain. --purge deletes them too: the ~/.kongtrol folder, Kongtrol's passwords in the keychain and the key that signs the audit log (plus the audit log or the --config file if you keep them in another folder); it cannot be undone. --data-only deletes the same, but leaves the app installed.

```text
kongtrol uninstall [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `--data-only` | delete the same as --purge, but keep the app installed |
| `--dry-run` | show what it would do, change nothing |
| `--purge` | also delete the ~/.kongtrol folder and the passwords saved in the keychain from this computer (cannot be undone) |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask (for scripts) |

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol uninstall --dry-run      # shows what it would do, changes nothing
kongtrol uninstall                # removes the app; your data stays on this computer
kongtrol uninstall --purge        # removes the app and deletes your data and passwords from this computer
```

### `kongtrol version`

Shows the installed Kongtrol version. To check the rest of your computer: kongtrol doctor.

```text
kongtrol version [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol version
kongtrol --version
kongtrol version --plain
```

### `kongtrol help`

Shows help for any command, with examples. Try: kongtrol help up.

```text
kongtrol help [command] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
kongtrol help
kongtrol help up
```

## Global flags

| Flags | Description |
|---|---|
| `-c, --config path` | config file path (default: ~/.kongtrol/kongtrol.yaml) |
| `-h, --help` | help for kongtrol |
| `--json` | emit JSON output for automation |
| `--plain` | plain ASCII output (no color and no Unicode symbols) |
| `-q, --quiet` | reduce non-essential output (no banner/spinner) |
| `-v, --version` | show the installed version and exit |

## Output language

Messages and help follow `KONGTROL_LANG`, then the language saved with `kongtrol config lang`, then the OS language (Spanish if the OS is in Spanish, English otherwise). For one run: `KONGTROL_LANG=es kongtrol --help`. `kongtrol config favorites|defaults|lang|dashboard` write to `~/.kongtrol/preferences.json` (this computer only), not `kongtrol.yaml`.
